speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To understand the origin of these symptoms, have you been in close contact with anyone who has had a similar rash or a known infection recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The classic progression you described—starting with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a facial rash that spares the perioral area—is highly specific for measles. I am requesting images of the rash to confirm the presence of Koplik spots or the characteristic confluent maculopapular pattern.
